title: The reading room
logline: The library's back room. Archive boxes. An empty chair — the librarian's. Wood as a reflection in the reading-room glass, and his own strips in a folder.

panels.composition: The town library's back room: metal shelves of archive boxes, a long table, a wooden chair with a cardigan on its back and no one in it, a green-shaded lamp. A folder open on the table: Timberline back pages, 1997–99, and a laundromat digest. In the glass of the reading-room door, faint: WOOD's reflection, looking at the folder. He is not in the room. He is in the glass.

characters.pose: a reflection in the door's glass

props: a folder of old back pages

image.prompt: a library back room with metal shelves of archive boxes, a long table under a green-shaded lamp, a wooden chair with a cardigan over its back and no one in it, an open folder of old newspaper comic pages, and in the glass of the door the faint reflection of a man looking at the folder, spare ink with muted ochre watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: Mrs. Gable's room, for the reader of vol 7 — never named. The cardigan on the chair is all the strip gives.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The echo room. The strip's own past in a folder. Wood in the glass.
